def.title: The Smuggler's Recipe
def.blurb: The night before the Harvest Fair, the Anchor's famous pie recipe vanishes from its frame behind the bar.

intro.text: Ned Polglase. I keep the Anchor. That card's hung behind my bar since before my grandad pulled his first pint.
The Smuggler's Pie. Written out in the 1890s. Every Harvest Fair we bake it from that very card.
And this morning the frame's empty?
Hung back up, neat as you like. Not a scratch on it. Just no recipe inside.
Mrrp. (Four little screws, all put back. A careful thief. A thief with a screwdriver.)

clue.title: Four Screws
clue.text: The frame was unscrewed with a small screwdriver and hung back up empty. No rush and no damage: whoever took the card took their time.

intro.text: Who was in the Anchor last night, Ned?
Quiz night. Mr Pellow, the Professor, Rafe, and Kit till ten. She had the night shift.
I was on the ward till seven this morning. Sister signed the ward book. Three new babies, no pie.
Mrow. (Kit left at ten. The frame was still full at last orders. Ned checked the till under it.)

clue.title: Last Orders
clue.text: The recipe was still in its frame at last orders. Kit had left at ten for her night shift at the cottage hospital, and the ward book has her there until seven.

intro.text: I set the quiz, so naturally I marked it. Question nine had three acceptable answers, and I footnoted all of them.
He was in the back room with me, marking, from last orders till I locked up. I couldn't get rid of him.
We left together. Ned locked the door behind us. I heard him rattle it twice.
Mrrp. (So the Professor was never alone near the bar. Who was?)

clue.title: The Quiz Sheets
clue.text: Quill marked the quiz with Ned in the back room from last orders until Ned locked up. They never left each other's sight, and left together.

intro.text: Yes, I'd love a smuggler's recipe. Wonderful story. Sells itself. But look at me.
Rafe's right wrist is in a sling. He slipped on the harbour steps on Tuesday, and Kit strapped it up.
That frame's above the top shelf. You'd need a stool, and two good hands for the screws.
Mrow. (One good hand. And he can't even open his own crisps.)

clue.title: Rafe's Sling
clue.text: Rafe's wrist has been in a sling since Tuesday. The frame hangs above the top shelf: whoever took the card stood on a stool and used both hands.

intro.text: Ned, is there a photo of the card? I'd like to see the writing.
On the menu. Look at those big looping P's. Pastry, pepper, pinch of mace.
Now that hand is familiar. I've seen those P's in the parish chest. A christening card, 1902.
Mrrp. (Whose christening? Who would know whose hand that is, just by looking?)

clue.title: The Handwriting
clue.text: The recipe's looping P's match a 1902 christening card for a Pellow baby. Only two people would know that hand on sight: a Pellow, or the village historian.

def.question: Who took the Smuggler's Pie recipe?

accusePrompt.text: Five clues, Biscuit. Who took the recipe?
Mrrp. (Who stayed after last orders, wasn't marking the quiz, had two good hands, and knew that writing?)

quill.text: Mrow. (Quill was marking the quiz with Ned until the door was locked. He was never alone by the bar.)

rafe.text: Mrow. (Rafe has one hand in a sling. You need two for those screws, and a stool.)

kit.text: Mrow. (Kit left at ten for the night shift. The recipe was still there at last orders.)

ending.text: Mr Pellow. You stayed after last orders, and you knew that writing the moment you saw it close up.
Aye. My granny's hand. Ellen Pellow. She cooked at the Anchor fifty years. That pie was hers.
A hundred years they've called it the smuggler's. Not one word of her. I wanted her name on it, that's all.
Then her name goes on it. Today. Why didn't you just say, you stubborn old haddock?
At the Harvest Fair, the pie is served as Granny Pellow's Pie, with Ellen's photo above the bar.
Purrr. (Granny Pellow made excellent pastry. I've checked. Twice.)
Biscuit, look at the calendar. Next month the Salt & Page will have been open a whole year.
Mrrp. (A birthday. For the shop, and therefore for me. I'll need a party.)
